children: Portugal sold a total of around €1.63 billion ($1.9 billion) of four-, eight- and nine-year bonds in an auction on Wednesday, state debt agency IGCP said, with yields rising from the previous sales.
The allotment yield on the nine-year bond, of which the IGCP sold €602 million, fetched 3.632%, up from 3.342% in an auction of a similar maturity in June.
The eight-year debt yielded 3.559%, up from 3.009% in an auction of a similar maturity in March, with €629 million worth placed.
The four-year debt yielded 3.122%, up from 2.834% in an auction of a similar maturity in May, with €400 million worth placed.
Demand exceeded the amount placed by 2.79 times on the four-year maturity, by 1.66 times on the eight-year maturity, and by 1.52 times on the nine-year maturity.
